links.reason: The StandardDistributions ownership paragraph explicitly delegates uniqueness from moments to OrthogonalL2Bases. B1 applies to an L1 density difference h with integral exp(a*abs(x))*abs(h(x)) finite for some a>0 and vanishing polynomial moments; it gives h=0 almost everywhere. A single positive a supports strip analyticity; all exponential moments support the stronger entire-function argument. The consumer must construct h from two densities against the same reference and prove the density-to-measure equality bridge. This is not determinacy from polynomial moments alone, and the stated B1 interface does not automatically cover discrete laws, arbitrary weak limits or the nondegenerate log-normal family. Attach the ownership directive to Layer 1, not to every scalar calculation.

links.reason: The nonzero-scale Cauchy non-integrability theorem supplies OptimalTransport Layer 3 item 2's concrete counterexample. For the probability law mu=cauchyMeasure x0 gamma with gamma nonzero, a finite second moment would imply integrability of id by L2-to-L1 inclusion, a contradiction. This duplicates an elementary law identity, not the full statistical and transport theories. StandardDistributions permits rectangular L and positive-semidefinite S. OptimalTransport additionally needs positive-definite square-root, inverse and geometric-mean identities and their transport applications.
overlaps.proposal: Keep the elementary affine-law and covariance-pushforward theorem in StandardDistributions Layer 5, on finite real Euclidean carriers with rectangular L and S.PosSemidef. Replace the duplicate law-building clause in OptimalTransport Layer 5 item 3 with an explicit import and carrier adapter. Keep the Brenier matrix, W2 formula, interpolation, barycenters and their positive-matrix identities in OptimalTransport; keep Cholesky, Wishart densities and conditional-Gaussian laws in StandardDistributions. Do not impose positive definiteness on the affine-law theorem or extend it to arbitrary totalized covariance parameters. Emit no edge for this pair until the ownership decision is accepted. Later transport examples use their local geometry/flow interfaces, not fresh whole-roadmap reverse dependencies.
